name: United Foods International (USA), Inc.
old_description: We have been a leading manufacturer of both liquid and dry products for decades. From sauces and soup bases to a variety of powder products, items manufactured at our facilities are in retailers and restaurants around the world.
about:
United Foods International (USA), Inc. traces its roots to 1988 when Senba USA, Inc. was founded in San Francisco as a base for manufacturing and selling condiments and spices. The company later adopted its current name and moved its U.S. headquarters to Hayward, California, where it operates a West Coast factory. Additional U.S. facilities were opened in Belcamp, Maryland (2016) and Phoenix, Arizona (2021).

The company specializes in custom manufacturing of liquid and dry food products, including sauces (BBQ, hot, Asian, dressings), soup bases (broth, ramen, vegan), seasonings, batter mixes, baking mixes, and drink mixes. Its processing capabilities cover liquid filling, retort stabilization, powder blending (including Nauta and tote blenders), powder filling and packaging, cartoning, powder granulation, bottling assembly, soft drink production, deep drawing, baking via tunnel ovens, freezing, and tableting. Three U.S. plants are complemented by a global network of facilities in Japan, China, Thailand, Singapore, and Indonesia.

United Foods serves retail, foodservice, industrial, and wholesale channels, providing private-label products that appear in retailers and restaurants worldwide. Customers range from brands seeking custom sauces and soup bases to those needing dry seasonings, breading, and batter mixes for retail or foodservice distribution.

The company emphasizes its in-house research and development team, which handles recipe formulation, ingredient sourcing, and commercialization, and its adherence to GFSI-benchmarked food safety standards (SQF and BRCGS). It also offers natural, organic, kosher, gluten-free, and non-GMO manufacturing, and notes that its varied dry-blender sizes allow smaller production runs without the high premiums typical of larger co-packers.
